lines.text: Every day, someone is supposed to summarize what changed in the project.
And every day, nobody does. Everyone is busy, and it gets forgotten.
An agent could write it in a minute, but only if somebody remembers to ask.
In Agent R Q, schedule the task on a cron, like every weekday at six.
The background poller watches the clock, and spawns the task for you.
At six o clock, a new run lands on your board, like any other task.
The agent starts working at once, even though nobody asked it. No reminder, no prompt, and no one has to be online.
It reads the commits and the tasks, and writes up what actually changed.
You can read the run, or reply to it, exactly like a normal task.
And every run stays on the board, so you build a history of every day. Over time, that becomes a searchable record of every single day.
No reminders, no chasing, and no more missed reports. The team just opens the board and reads yesterday's summary.
What report do you always forget to write? Tell us below, or try it at Agent R Q dot com.
